title: FSAs Explained: Contribution Limits, Deadlines, and What Happens If You Don't Spend It
metaDescription: How Flexible Spending Accounts work, 2025-2026 contribution limits, and the deadlines that decide if you lose unused money.
bodyHtml:
A Flexible Spending Account (FSA) is one of the easiest ways to lower your taxable income, but it's also one of the easiest benefits to mess up. If you don't understand the deadlines, you can hand money back to your employer for no reason. Here's how FSAs actually work and how to avoid losing what you set aside.

What an FSA Actually Is

An FSA is a pretax account offered through an employer. You elect an amount at open enrollment, and it's deducted from your paycheck in equal installments before taxes are calculated. With a flexible spending account, your contributions can be used to pay for certain out-of-pocket health care costs for you, your spouse, and your dependents.
